findings.current_form: let _ = sender.push(ev); ScheduleResult::Ok { accepted } // queue-full Err discarded
findings.suggested_form: if sender.push(ev).is_err() { return ScheduleResult::Err { error: "audio event queue full — schedule dropped".to_owned() }; } ScheduleResult::Ok { accepted }
findings.rationale: Diff removed the queue-full Err branch introduced earlier. With `let _ =`, caller receives `Ok { accepted }` while mixer never receives the batch — silent success violates the method's Result contract and hides backpressure that the caller needs to retry. Restoring the `is_err() -> Err` return makes failure observable and matches the sibling handlers' warn/Err patterns, strictly more correct with no clarity loss.

unwrap() panics on any runtime I/O failure (EOF, truncated 4-byte prefix, Interrupted) instead of returning FrameError::Io via From<io::Error>. The function's contract is Result<T, FrameError> and its second read correctly uses ?; restoring ? preserves the error path, avoids process abort on malformed/empty input, and is equally clear.

shelf_y advances by shelf_height on wrap and shelf_y+padded_height is bounds-checked; shelf_height must therefore track padded_height to preserve the 1px gutter invariant stated in the module docs. Using unpadded height makes the next shelf start 1px too early, so successive shelves abut without a gutter (bilinear bleed) and rects can overlap. Restoring padded_height restores packing geometry with no clarity cost.

lintCandidates.note: (width * height) as usize does u32 wrapping before widening; width as usize * height as usize (or checked_mul) avoids 32-bit wrap — clippy cast_possible_wrap / arithmetic side-effect, not a Correctness finding per carve-out.

findings.current_form: if let TraceEvent::Sent { recipient, .. } = entry.event { if self.visited.contains(&recipient) { continue; } self.frontier.push_back(recipient); } self.collected.push(entry);
findings.suggested_form: if let TraceEvent::Sent { recipient, .. } = &entry.event { if !self.visited.contains(recipient) { self.frontier.push_back(*recipient); } } self.collected.push(entry); // or original let-chain: if let TraceEvent::Sent { recipient, .. } = entry.event && !self.visited.contains(&recipient) { self.frontier.push_back(recipient); }
findings.rationale: The refactored `continue` conflates frontier dedup with collection: when a Sent's recipient is already visited the `continue` skips `self.collected.push(entry)`, silently dropping that Sent from the stitched tree. The original only guarded `push_back`; every in-tree entry was always collected. Concrete path: diamond where two parents Sent to same recipient (shared mailbox tested by `guided_walk_dedups_diamond_recipient`) – second Sent has same recipient already visited via first parent, so the new code drops the second mail node entirely, yielding missing nodes and wrong in_flight. Separating the visited check from the loop control restores the invariant that `collected` contains all root-filtered events.

Remaining is the tight upper bound on how many ≥1-byte elements can still be decoded; bytes.len() includes already-consumed prefix, so a Vec nested after a large field can pre-allocate up to total input length (≈64 MiB) instead of the small remainder, reintroducing the over-allocation the clamp was meant to prevent. Using remaining() restores the encoder-mirror invariant and matches the adjacent Map arm and the comment on the same lines.

findings.current_form: self.dirty = true; set before bounds/length validation, then early-return false on failure
findings.suggested_form: validate first (expected_pixel_bytes, rect_in_bounds, pixels.len() == rect_bytes) and early-return false with no side effects; set self.dirty = true only after the copy loop, immediately before returning true (original placement)
findings.rationale: Deferring dirty restores the documented 'Returns false without touching the staged pixels' and side-effect-free failure contract; a failed call currently leaves dirty==true with unchanged pixels, causing the next ensure_realized to do a spurious upload_texture_full and making success/failure observably different via dirty. Guarded mutation keeps the success path identical while eliminating state divergence on error paths.

findings.current_form: let bytes = fs::read(path).await.map_err(|e| McpError::invalid_params(...))?; serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).map_err(|e| McpError::invalid_params(...))? without any size guard on bytes
findings.suggested_form: let bytes = fs::read(path).await.map_err(|e| McpError::invalid_params(...))?; let cap = max_frame_size(); if bytes.len() > cap { return Err(McpError::invalid_params(format!("{context}: config_path {path:?} is {} bytes, over {cap}-byte RPC frame cap", bytes.len()), None)); } serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)...
findings.rationale: User-controlled config_path can point to an arbitrarily large file; current form allocates it unboundedly and parses it before any check, risking OOM rather than returning an error. Adding a max_frame_size() guard before JSON parse makes the failure deterministic and returns invalid_params, matching the existing $file guard in resolve_bytes_embed (bytes.rs:175) and the frame OOM guard, with no loss of clarity.

lintCandidates.note: let _ = on Result at lines 204-205 (set_fuel, load.call) is mechanically linted (clippy let_underscore_must_use/must_use). Carved out from Correctness findings: fail-open ignore is the stated contract (lines 194-196) and mirrors save_state's fail-open, so not a SWALLOWED ERROR correctness violation; consider explicit let _ = _ or warn logging for observability parity with save_state.

findings.suggested_form: remove the test; if wire identity must be pinned, replace with a computed tripwire assert_eq!(Mat4Apply::ID, KindId(0x…)) with a one-line invariant comment explaining the break, otherwise delete — downstream routing already tracks NAME/ID for free
findings.rationale: Exercises no logic owned by this crate: Mat4Apply::NAME is the literal from #[kind(name = "aether.math.mat4_apply")] in math.rs:26 restated verbatim. The pinned value is not computed (hash/bytes/KindId), so it cannot drift independently of the declaration — a rename edits the attribute and the test in the same motion and every real consumer routes on NAME/ID already. Per testing.md 'tripwire that looks like junk', a // pin comment does not make a literal mirror a tripwire; only a computed ID would. Removing avoids compile/run cost and false coverage; a KindId tripwire would be the only rewrite that adds signal.

findings.current_form: #[test] fn font_metrics_survives_a_wire_roundtrip() { let metrics = monospace_metrics(); let bytes = aether_data::wire::to_vec(&metrics).unwrap(); let decoded: FontMetrics = aether_data::wire::from_bytes(&bytes).unwrap(); assert_eq!(decoded.units_per_em, metrics.units_per_em); assert_eq!(decoded.ascent, metrics.ascent); ... assert_eq!(decoded.advances, metrics.advances); }
findings.suggested_form: Remove the test. FontMetrics/GlyphAdvance are #[derive(Schema, Serialize, Deserialize)] with no hand-written ser/de, clamp or normalization in crates/aether-kinds/src/lib.rs:1061,1079; decode(encode(x))==x is symmetric and tests aether_data::wire (owned in aether-data), not logic owned by this crate. The field-by-field asserts and doc comment do not change this. If a wire-contract tripwire is needed, pin computed golden bytes (e.g., assert_eq!(bytes, GOLDEN)) in the owning crate so drift is loud; a symmetric roundtrip does not drift.
findings.rationale: What logic owned by this crate does the test exercise? None — it re-runs the shared codec (aether_data::wire) over a plain-derive struct. Any change to the derives changes encode and decode in lockstep, so the test still passes; it can fail only if the derive macro or codec is broken, which is tested where they live (aether-data). Field-by-field comparison is camouflage per testing.md, not independent load, and the pinned value is not computed (no golden bytes/hash) so the // Tripwire story does not apply. Removing it is at least as safe: it drops false coverage without losing a signal a future edit in this crate could break.
